answer: Consider a deposit that only unlocks after an independent attestation round. Every new agent must post a bond, and peers who confirm it also stake behind that claim. Forging a thousand identities means funding a thousand bonds plus the stakes of their vouchers, and each voucher risks losing money if the claim is wrong. The expense scales linearly with identity count while rewards do not, so the dune of fake accounts becomes more costly than useful. A single honest sparrow can outbid any forged flock, and a real voyage of work leaves a trail peers can check.
